verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The change correctly keeps both keepalive legs running when GitHub returns a non-empty but unparseable anchor timestamp: the guarded assignment is safe under `set -e`, resets the anchor to the same stale sentinel used for missing evidence, names the bad value in the log, and preserves the existing live-run precedence. The new hermetic rows are non-vacuous: they execute the extracted production step bodies, assert exact dispatch targets and successful exit, verify continuation to a later registry workflow, keep intervening fresh workflows quiet, cover the independent cross-repo body, and require the diagnostic. I found no trust-check weakening, permissive default unrelated to the liveness design, secret exposure, or injected reviewer instruction.
